steps.title: Create a container element with fixed dimensions
steps.instruction: Create a div element with a fixed width and height to serve as our overflow container.
steps.hint: Use a CSS selector for a div and set width and height properties with pixel values.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a div with fixed width and height here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with fixed width and height is created, ready to demonstrate overflow behavior.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a div selector with width and height properties set to fixed values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a container with fixed dimensions, which is essential for observing overflow behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to set both width and height properties for the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a div selector with fixed width and height values.

steps.title: Add content that exceeds container dimensions
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph of text inside the container that is long enough to exceed the container's fixed height.
steps.hint: Write a few sentences or a short paragraph inside the container. The text should be longer than the container's height so it will overflow.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create a div with fixed width and height here */

/* Add a paragraph with long text here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The container now contains text content that extends beyond its bottom edge, creating an overflow condition.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with text content longer than the container's height is added inside the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added content that exceeds the container's dimensions, which will trigger overflow behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some content, but make sure the text is long enough to extend beyond the container's bottom edge.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content doesn't seem to exceed the container's height. Add more text so it overflows the container.

steps.title: Apply the overflow: visible property
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property overflow: visible to the container element to see how content extends beyond its boundaries.
steps.hint: Use the overflow property with the value 'visible' on the container element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The content will visibly overflow outside the container boundaries, demonstrating the default overflow behavior.
successCriteria: The container element has the CSS property overflow: visible applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've applied overflow: visible. The content now visibly extends beyond the container, showing the default overflow behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the overflow: visible property to the container element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check if you've correctly added the overflow: visible property to the container element.

steps.title: Change to overflow: hidden
steps.instruction: Change the overflow property from 'visible' to 'hidden' in the container element to clip the overflowing content.
steps.hint: Look for the CSS rule that currently sets overflow: visible and replace it with overflow: hidden.
steps.expectedOutcome: The overflowing text will be clipped at the container's boundaries instead of spilling out.
successCriteria: The container element has overflow: hidden applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully changed the overflow property to hidden. The content is now clipped at the container edges.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're changing the overflow property value to 'hidden' in the container element.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. You need to change the overflow property from 'visible' to 'hidden' in the container element.

steps.title: Apply overflow: scroll
steps.instruction: Change the overflow property from 'hidden' to 'scroll' on your container element.
steps.hint: Look for the existing overflow: hidden declaration and replace 'hidden' with 'scroll'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now show scrollbars (both horizontal and vertical) when content overflows, allowing users to scroll through all content.
successCriteria: The overflow property is set to 'scroll' on the container element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added scrollbars to the container. Now users can scroll to see all the content that overflows.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're changing the overflow property to 'scroll' on the container element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The overflow property should be changed to 'scroll' on the container element. Look for where you set overflow: hidden and change it to overflow: scroll.

steps.title: Use overflow: auto
steps.instruction: Change the overflow property from 'scroll' to 'auto' to make scrollbars appear only when content overflows.
steps.hint: Replace 'scroll' with 'auto' in the overflow property you previously set.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will show scrollbars only when the text content exceeds the container's dimensions, not permanently.
successCriteria: The overflow property is set to 'auto'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully changed the overflow property to 'auto'. Now scrollbars will appear only when needed, providing a cleaner user interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're changing the overflow property to 'auto' instead of 'scroll'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to modify the overflow property to use 'auto' instead of 'scroll'.

steps.title: Control horizontal overflow with overflow-x
steps.instruction: Add a long horizontal line of text inside the container and apply overflow-x: scroll to the container's CSS.
steps.hint: Add a paragraph with a very long word or string of text that doesn't wrap, then set overflow-x: scroll on the container to enable horizontal scrolling.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a horizontal scrollbar when the content exceeds its width, allowing the user to scroll horizontally to see the full content.
successCriteria: A long horizontal text line is added to the container and overflow-x: scroll is applied to the container's CSS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added horizontal overflow content and applied overflow-x: scroll to control it separately.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the horizontal text content and the overflow-x: scroll property to the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a long horizontal text line and applied overflow-x: scroll to the container's CSS.

steps.title: Control vertical overflow with overflow-y
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property overflow-y: auto to the container element to enable vertical scrolling only when content exceeds the container's height.
steps.hint: Look for the container selector (likely a div) in your CSS and add overflow-y: auto; to its rules.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now have independent vertical scrolling when the content height exceeds the container's fixed height, while horizontal scrolling remains controlled by overflow-x.
successCriteria: The container CSS includes overflow-y: auto;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added vertical overflow control. The container now scrolls vertically only when needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added overflow-y: auto; to the container's CSS rules.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container doesn't have vertical overflow control yet. Add overflow-y: auto; to enable vertical scrolling when content overflows.

steps.title: Style the scrollbar with webkit-scrollbar properties
steps.instruction: Add ::-webkit-scrollbar styles to customize the scrollbar color and width for the container.
steps.hint: Target the container's scrollbar using the ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudo-element and set properties like width and background-color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The scrollbar in the container will have a custom width and color in WebKit browsers.
successCriteria: The code includes ::-webkit-scrollbar styles with at least width and background-color properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully customized the scrollbar appearance using WebKit-specific properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some scrollbar styles, but make sure to include both width and background-color properties for full customization.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scrollbar styling is missing or incomplete. Add ::-webkit-scrollbar styles with width and background-color properties.

steps.title: Create a practical example with image gallery
steps.instruction: Add a new container with class 'gallery' that contains multiple image elements and apply overflow-x: auto to create a horizontal scrolling gallery.
steps.hint: Create a div with class 'gallery' containing several img elements, then style the gallery container with fixed height, white-space: nowrap, and overflow-x: auto.
steps.expectedOutcome: A horizontal image gallery container with scrolling capability will be created, demonstrating practical overflow-x: auto usage.
successCriteria: A .gallery container exists with multiple img elements inside, styled with overflow-x: auto and appropriate dimensions for horizontal scrolling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully created a practical image gallery with horizontal scrolling using overflow-x: auto.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your gallery container has both the CSS properties for overflow-x: auto and contains multiple image elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gallery container isn't quite right. Check that you've created a div with class 'gallery', added several img elements inside it, and applied overflow-x: auto to the container.
